html:
The Slovak National Uprising was an armed revolt against the Slovak State and Nazi Germany, launched on 29 August 1944 from Banská Bystrica in central Slovakia.

Army officers, communists and democrats planned it together, hoping to join the advancing Red Army. Parts of the Slovak army and partisans held central Slovakia for two months. But the Soviet push through the Carpathians stalled at the Dukla Pass, and German troops crushed the revolt by late October. Reprisals killed thousands, among them many Jews and Roma. The uprising let Slovaks claim a place among the victors and shaped the postwar settlement of Czechoslovakia. Its anniversary is a public holiday in Slovakia.
sum: The Slovak National Uprising was an armed revolt against the Slovak State and Nazi Germany, launched on 29 August 1944 from Banská Bystrica in central Slovakia.
